evidence.text: Grains of sand; 小 provides the pronunciation and meaning
Pictograph of four small dots, representing grains of sand or rice, to convey the meaning "less". Similar to 小.
不多也。从小丿聲。

Pictogram (象形) – four dots, perhaps three grains of sand (see 沙), to indicate "a few, a little". Phonetically borrowed from 小 (OC *smewʔ, “small”), which is depicted by three dots.
Unrelated to 步 (and hence 歲), in which the lower component is the stylization of a foot.
不多也。从小丿聲。
few, less, inadequate

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese University of Hong Kong)
evidence.text: The entry says oracle-bone spellings of 少 and 小 were not reliably distinguished by three versus four dots and were used for both ‘small’ and ‘few’. It reports that bronze forms add a 丿-like stroke to the 小-shaped graph; cited bronze examples use 少 for ‘few’ in contrast with 多 and also for ‘young’, while some still use it for 小. The entry treats the graphs as an early shared form that later differentiated, and gives the Shuowen analysis 从小丿聲 as a historical account.
evidence.title: 漢字甲骨部件分析：小

evidence.source: 中央研究院 漢字構形資料庫 (Academia Sinica Character Database)
evidence.text: The entry describes 少 and 小 as originally one graph, picturing fine sand grains with the sense ‘tiny’; by the bronze-inscription period, the bottom dot of 少 had become a slanting stroke, distinguishing it from 小. The page lists oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen form categories, but its individual image records are not transcribed in the accessible text.
evidence.title: 漢字「少」：字形演變

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education)
evidence.field: 說文釋形; 字樣說明; 釋義
evidence.text: The dictionary records Shuowen’s account: ‘不多也。从小，丿聲’ (‘not many; from 小, with 丿 as phonetic’), and notes the seal-script form. It gives modern readings shǎo and shào, with senses including ‘not many’, ‘short time’, ‘insufficient/missing’, and ‘young/youthful’ under the departing-tone reading. Its cited examples include Mencius for ‘not few’ and Mozi for ‘young’.
evidence.title: A01069 少 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 段玉裁《說文解字注》, accessed via Shuowen.org
evidence.text: Shuowen glosses 少 as ‘not many’ and parses it 从小丿聲. Duan Yucai explains that what is not many is small, so 少 and 小 were mutually glossed in old usage. He comments that the phonetic analysis may be based on ancient initial-consonant relations. This is evidence for the received Shuowen and Qing commentary, not direct confirmation of the graph’s original design.
evidence.title: 說文解字「少」

evidence.source: Nohara Masaki, ‘The reconstruction of the word shao (少) in Old Chinese Phonology’
evidence.field: sections 2.2–3.1; table 2; discussion of oracle-bone, bronze and manuscript usage
evidence.text: The 2015 study surveys competing phonological analyses. It reports Zhengzhang and Pan analyses that connect 少 to the 明母 series, with Zhengzhang proposing an intermediate nasal relationship to 小; it reports that Schuessler and Baxter–Sagart do not accept the 少–眇 relationship and consequently do not accept 小 as a phonetic relative in that series. The author finds early spelling usage complex: oracle-bone forms conventionally transcribed 少 or 小 can represent either ‘few’ or ‘small’; cited examples include oracle-bone Heji 12711 and 33920, Chu manuscripts, and Qin slips. The study says Qin usage distinguishes 少 from 小, but the precise point when the distinction became stable is uncertain. It also notes that the received Shuowen assigns phonetic status to 丿, not 小. This leaves historical sound-series claims disputed and does not establish that 小 was the phonetic element of the original graph.
evidence.title: 「少」の上古音再構について

evidence.field: Old Chinese reconstruction table; entries for 少
evidence.text: The authors’ table presents distinct Baxter–Sagart Middle Chinese transcription and Old Chinese reconstruction columns. The local table rows supplied with this dossier give 少 shǎo, MC syewX, OC *[s.t]ewʔ (‘few’) and 少 shào, MC syewH, OC *[s-t]ewʔ-s (‘young’). These exact local rows agree with the reconstructions cited in the 2015 study’s comparison table in broad substance, though its compact printed transcription differs in typography. These are reconstructed readings of 少, not proof that 小 was its phonetic component.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The disagreement over 少's original graph remains: one database interprets early forms as fine sand grains and a shared 少/小 graph; early usage data confirms spelling overlap but does not independently prove the depicted referent was sand, rice, or another object. No glyph image was visually inspected.

The component analysis is not settled. Shuowen says 小 is semantic and 丿 phonetic; modern accounts also propose a shared, originally undivided graph. The 2015 phonology study documents disagreement over whether 少 and 小 are historically phonologically connected. Local pronunciation rows alone cannot establish a phonetic role.

Chronological glossing is not warranted from dictionary order. Early epigraphic/manuscript examples support contexts for ‘small’ and ‘few’; bronze examples are also reported for ‘young’. The available material does not establish a secure step-by-step semantic path from ‘small’ to ‘few’, ‘insufficient’, ‘short time’, or ‘young’.

The received source packet’s ‘four grains’ explanation is not independently established as a literal depiction. One source calls the shared graph sand-grains, while another presents the four-dot description as a possibility; there is no independently recoverable name or pronunciation of a depicted object to evaluate a borrowing claim.

The exact official Unihan character records for 少 and 小 could not be accessed. The local dossier row for 少 is shǎo, but no external official character-page confirmation was obtained; no 小 reading was established here.

The local Baxter–Sagart file is not an external URL and its provenance row was provided by the harness. The authors’ online table was inspected, but searchable page extraction did not expose the exact 少 row; supplied local values are therefore reported with their source limitation.

Search access to the Academia Sinica bronze corpus timed out. The evidence reviewed does not establish a precise earliest dated attestation for the character itself or a fully documented dated sequence for its senses.
The competing early-dot interpretations remain unresolved: sources describe smallness or fine sand grains, but the original depicted referent is not independently recoverable.

The early graphic overlap of 少 and 小 is supported by the inspected specialist pages; the stage when their use became consistently differentiated is not securely dated here. Bronze usage is reported for ‘few’, ‘young’, and sometimes ‘small’.

The Shuowen analysis 从小丿聲 is a received historical account. Competing paleographic interpretations treat 少 and 小 as an early shared graph; the material reviewed does not establish 丿 as the original phonetic component or 小 as the original sound component.
The semantic relations among early ‘small’, ‘few’, ‘young’, ‘insufficient’, and ‘short time’ are not established as a chronological chain. Dictionary ordering is not used as chronology.

No exact earliest dated attestation or independently dated staged sequence of senses was verified. The specialist page provides inscription citations and object names but this pass did not verify their dates against primary corpus records.

Current Mandarin and Baxter–Sagart local rows for 少 were supplied in the dossier. The component 小 exact local reading row was not supplied; official Unihan individual character pages were not rechecked in this pass, so no component sound array or official Unihan claim is made.

The direct image fetch endpoint returned a cache-miss error after Commons linked it. The exact URL was nevertheless obtained from the opened file description page. The selected image is a modern SVG redraw of a Shang oracle-script form, not a photograph of an excavated artifact.
No Xiaoxuetang 少-specific form was selected because this search did not yield a verified record page with exact direct glyph URL.

External official Unihan records for 少 and 丿 could not be inspected. The exact local Unihan rows supplied by the harness are 少 shǎo and 丿 piě; this comparison may be recorded as local metadata but must not be presented as externally verified official-page evidence.

The current Mandarin comparison piě–shǎo does not resolve the historical phonetic proposal 丿聲. The received Shuowen account supports reporting that proposal; a modern reading pair is not evidence of its ancient sound relation.

Exact 少 and 小 Baxter–Sagart rows were supplied locally and checked against the dossier’s component and host characters, but the inspected publisher page did not expose those rows. The disputed historical sound-series interpretations remain distinct from the phonetic role assigned to 丿 in Shuowen.

Official Unihan per-character pages for 丿, 少 and 小 were inaccessible in this run. The local dataset rows for 丿 piě and 少 shǎo are provided data, not externally verified page contents; do not claim those pages were inspected.
The modern Mandarin pair piě–shǎo does not establish the received Shuowen phonetic analysis 丿聲 or an ancient sound relationship.

The candidate seal radical file pages for 丿 and 小 were inaccessible. The inspected 小-seal.svg page describes a modern redraw and has mixed rights statements; it adds no direct evidence about 少’s graphic development.

The selected 少 oracle-style illustration is a modern vector redraw rather than an artifact photograph. Its specific depicted specimen has no independent artifact date; the actual direct image fetch returned a cache miss after Commons exposed its URL.
